title: The Songbook of the Crescent Cove
premise: Wren Voss has spent ten years writing anonymous letters to the lighthouse at Crescent Cove, never knowing they were answered by Theo Marsh, a composer who inherited the neighboring cottage and fell in love with her words before her face. When Theo finally moves in full-time to finish a symphony he can no longer hear clearly—his hearing is failing—he recognizes Wren's handwriting on a scrap of manuscript paper, and their parallel secrets collide. As Wren's debut novel deadline looms and Theo races to notate his final movement, they must decide whether love built on borrowed anonymity can survive being fully seen. The story ends with Wren reading her published dedication aloud in the lighthouse gallery while Theo, nearly deaf, feels the words through her hand on his chest.
about_author: O. M. Sandoval is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent years cataloguing letters found in coastal lighthouses. They write from a converted boathouse on the Atlantic, where they insist the tide sets their writing schedule.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Returning to Crescent Cove to settle her late grandfather's estate, Wren finds his ledger filled with replies to letters she never sent under her own name—letters she wrote anonymously for a decade. She realizes someone answered every one. Emotional beat: unsettled longing; the past is more alive than she believed.

chapters.title: The Neighbor with the Piano Crate
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo Marsh moves into the adjacent cottage with crates of sheet music and a hearing diagnosis he hides from everyone. He recognizes the new neighbor's handwriting instantly but says nothing, terrified the real Wren will eclipse the woman in the letters. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by fear of exposure.

chapters.title: Salt and Manuscript Paper
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm strands them together in the lighthouse; Wren sketches characters aloud while Theo hums an unfinished melody. Their creative kinship sparks, but each guards their secret. Emotional beat: magnetic connection built on mutual concealment.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Signed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Digging through her grandfather's things, Wren discovers the ledger's replies were written in two hands—her grandfather's early ones, then Theo's after his first visit ten years ago. She tests Theo by quoting a line from her own letter. His reaction confirms it. Emotional beat: vertigo of recognition.

chapters.title: The Movement He Can't Hear
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's audiologist delivers grim news: his usable hearing window is months, not years. He must finish the symphony now, and it was always meant as a reply to her letters. He begins orchestrating her words without telling her. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening devotion into desperation.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Theo about the letters; he confesses everything except his deafness, ashamed it makes him the 'broken' keeper of her words. Feeling deceived about identity rather than intent, Wren retreats to her novel deadline. Emotional beat: betrayal entangled with tenderness.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Bad Timing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo plays Wren the symphony's first movement—her decade of letters set to music—at a village concert. Mid-performance his hearing cuts out; he finishes from memory and muscle alone. Wren, in the audience, understands what the music cost him. Emotional beat: awe cracking open forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Dedication Page
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Facing her publisher's final deadline, Wren rewrites her novel's ending to tell the truth she couldn't say aloud, dedicating it to 'the one who answered.' She asks Theo to read the draft—but he admits he may soon be unable to read her words at all. Emotional beat: grief and resolve braided together.

chapters.title: Crescendo in a Rising Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A hurricane forces them into the lighthouse as Theo's final pages scatter. Wren catches them against the wind while he dictates the last bars from memory, her hand pressed to his throat to feel the notes. Climax: choosing each other with no guarantees left. Emotional beat: fierce, unguarded love.

chapters.title: The Songbook of the Crescent Cove
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, Wren reads her published dedication aloud in the lighthouse gallery, Theo's palm flat against her chest to feel the words vibrate. The symphony premieres with a program note crediting 'ten years of unsigned letters.' Emotional beat: belonging fully earned; memory inherited forward.
